title: flaky: test_client_start_happy_path sees another test's Popen argv under pytest-randomly
body:
## Symptom

`tests/test_mcp_client_parity_v4_169_39.py::test_client_start_happy_path` fails depending on test execution order:

```
AssertionError: assert ['/Users/runn..., '--version'] == ['node', 'server.js']
```

The test patches `mcp_mod.subprocess.Popen` with a recorder, constructs `McpStdioClient("node", ["server.js"])`, and asserts the recorded argv. Instead of its own arguments it receives an argv ending in `--version` from an unrelated caller.

Observed on CI in the `Tests (Python 3.12 on macos-latest)` cell of PR #205, where it turned a required job red. The same commit passed on every Linux and Windows cell.

## Reproduced on the operator's Windows host

```
alone, -p no:randomly                        rc=0   passes
tests/e2e/test_bridge_live.py then this test rc=1   fails
whole file, --randomly-seed=1 / 2 / 3        rc=1   fails
```

The suite runs with **pytest-randomly**, so the order differs per run and per platform. That is why this surfaces on one matrix cell at a time and looks intermittent.

## Not caused by PR #205

Verified by removing that branch's files and re-running:

```
WITHOUT scripts/openapi_parity_ratchet.py,
        tests/test_openapi_parity_204.py,
        arena/public/openapi.py   -- seeds 1, 2, 3  -> all still rc=1
```

Identical failure without any of the changed files. `test_mcp_client_parity_v4_169_39.py` contains no reference to `openapi`, `route_registry`, `exec/script` or `token/regenerate`.

## Likely cause

`tests/e2e/test_bridge_live.py` is the other place in the suite that drives `Popen` with a `--version` argv. The recorded value leaking into an unrelated test points at module-level state that outlives the test which created it: a `Popen` patch applied outside `monkeypatch`, or a client/proc object cached on the module and reused.

Worth checking whether the shared object is `mcp_mod.subprocess` itself — if one test replaces the attribute without `monkeypatch`, every later test in the same process sees the replacement.

## Why it matters beyond the flake

This is a green-when-broken failure mode in the opposite direction: the test is correct and the *harness* is wrong, so the signal is noise. Related to #181 (same-SHA red-to-green flips are timing races, not test order) — the same class of defect, different mechanism. A required job that fails on one matrix cell for reasons unrelated to the change teaches everyone to re-run rather than read, which is how a genuine failure eventually gets waved through.

## Acceptance

- The test passes under any `--randomly-seed`, and after `tests/e2e/test_bridge_live.py` in the same process.
- Whatever global is leaking is restored by the test that sets it, via `monkeypatch` or an explicit fixture teardown.
- Sabotage: reintroduce the leak, the test must fail deterministically rather than depending on order.
